answer: Every payout address must name a distinct legal person. The registry reads filings, then walks beneficial-owner, bank and director records; identities sharing a director, an office or an account collapse into one unit: the veil is pierced at the bank, not the key. A thousand keys can sing one sonnet, yet they file as one company. A beacon marks any cluster whose ownership graph reconverges under a saffron-thin disclosure threshold; the cluster forfeits together. Scaling means a thousand real firms, each with audited accounts, a liable director and its own bank, kept apart for years.
